--- ## What does this Google Antigravity plugin do? `agy-dart` is a performance, KV-cache, and context-window plugin for **Google Antigravity** (also supports DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, and Codex via `--target`). It reduces repeated reads and large tool results, shows prompt-cache usage, and helps you resume work in a new chat when a session fills up or stalls. Once installed, it runs automatically in the background — no new commands to learn, just chat and code as usual: ### 1. Combine actions When the AI needs to search several terms, it runs them in one batch; when it edits multiple files, it edits them together and runs tests in the same step instead of resending your full chat context across half a dozen turns. ### 2. Block noise If a test run prints 3,000 lines of logs, the plugin passes only the lines that matter to the AI (e.g., line 42 failed, the other 199 passed) and stores the full log locally for lookup. On multi-thousand-line code files, it pulls the outline first and reads only the target lines. ### 3. Cache monitoring and optional keepalive The plugin stabilizes controllable client-side prefixes and reduces repeated reads of unchanged files; actual cache hit rates still depend on how the host constructs requests and on backend caching behavior (if you use a dynamic proxy pool, pinning a single exit node can serve as a controlled troubleshooting experiment). Automatic keepalive and desktop expiry alerts start off. If you enable keepalive, the initial limit is one ping per chat until your next message. You can change the limit in the panel. ### 4. Side panel & crash/hang rescue The right-sidebar panel shows: remaining context space, minutes until cache expiry, and total noise blocked. With multiple project windows open, if a background window is nearly out of context or stuck spinning with zero output, a desktop popup names that exact project and chat — click the popup to jump straight there. If a session crashes from blown-out context or hangs completely, click once in the panel to copy a progress summary and paste it into a new chat to continue. ### Other built-in features 1. **Restore context clues after `/compact`**: Records modified files, latest test/build pass status, and saved reference IDs in the background so the AI can pick back up right after `/compact`. 2. **Local search for long docs & web pages**: Stores multi-thousand-word docs or web pages by section in a local database and fetches only matching sections by keyword. 3. **Local script filtering for giant logs & tables**: On multi-MB logs, CSVs, or huge JSON dumps, the AI runs a short local script to compute counts or extract rows (e.g., top 5 failing endpoints) and returns only the result; large JSON outputs also surface error rows automatically. 4. **Workspace layout on new chats**: Supplies a compact directory, script, and core-file summary at the start of a new conversation. 5. **Loop warnings**: Shows a UI-only note (not injected into model context) when the AI repeats `edit → fail → revert → fail` cycles or calls the same tool with no progress. 6. **Secret masking & sensitive-file blocking**: Masks API keys and tokens in logs or fetched pages, blocks accidental reads of `.env` files when configured, and sandboxes read-only `git` queries against untrusted `.git/config` hooks. 7. **Hard 8.8 KB response cap with dynamic quota**: Antigravity spills tool outputs above ~10 KB into a temp file that costs an extra read turn; all plugin responses stay within 8.8 KB, dynamically giving short passing checks' unused space to failing stack traces. 8. **Detailed panel breakdown & offline simulation**: Inspect context usage across file reads, terminal output, and subagents, check 15-turn cache hit trends and miss causes, optionally read only changed lines after edits (off by default), or replay past chat history via CLI to measure cache hit rates and keepalive cost. 9. **Works smoothly alongside your Skills, plus a Skills bloat check**: Use it with any Skills in Antigravity, Claude Code, or Codex — your Skills guide the workflow while `agy-dart` quietly blocks giant file reads, trims noisy logs, and looks after your cache; run `node bin/agy-dart.mjs audit skills` to see how much startup context each installed Skill uses and spot oversized main files. > Antigravity updates frequently — click **Star** at the top right to follow compatibility updates. --- ## How to Install Use **Node.js 22.16.0 or later in the 22.x line, or Node.js 24 or later**. The installer checks that the built-in SQLite supports FTS5 with the trigram tokenizer. The plugin uses only built-in modules. ### Option 1: One-line terminal install (no clone needed) **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zou172866/Antigravity-agy-dart/v1.7.8/install.ps1 | iex ``` **macOS / Linux:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zou172866/Antigravity-agy-dart/v1.7.8/install.sh | sh ``` ### Option 2: Let Antigravity install it Send this to Antigravity: ```text Clone tag v1.7.8 of https://github.com/zou172866/Antigravity-agy-dart.git to a temp folder, run `node scripts/install.mjs install` (add `--install-rg` on Windows if `rg` is missing), and confirm `doctor` passes. ``` ### Option 3: Clone & install with custom flags ```powershell git clone --branch v1.7.8 --depth 1 https://github.com/zou172866/Antigravity-agy-dart.git cd Antigravity-agy-dart # Windows PowerShell (optional -InstallRg auto-installs ripgrep) .\install.ps1 -InstallRg # macOS / Linux ./install.sh ``` **Other commands:** ```bash node scripts/install.mjs install # Global install (auto-syncs GEMINI_HOME & T3 ACP if present) node scripts/install.mjs install --project /repo/path # Single-project install node scripts/install.mjs doctor # Check install health node scripts/install.mjs uninstall # Uninstall ``` Restart or reload Antigravity after installing and open a new chat. User-created `rules/*.local.md` files inside the plugin directory are preserved across upgrades. If you previously installed standalone `agy-fast` or `antigravity-plugin-context-mode`, disable the old ones in your plugin list. Indexed content and usage history are stored locally in `~/.agy-dart/context.db` by default and survive uninstall. Before uninstalling, `ctx_purge` can clear the current chat's index. When the host omits a session ID, this covers anonymous data for the confirmed workspace. To clear indexed data and history across all projects, call `ctx_purge` with `scope: "all"`. Global uninstall also removes the Gemini/T3 copies recorded by the installer. If an older copy has no ownership record, the installer prints its location and a command for removing that copy explicitly. --- ## Settings Automatic cache warming is off by default. To turn it on for a chat, enable **Auto-Keepalive** in the **agy-dart Context** panel — or click **Warm 1×** next to the countdown anytime for a single manual ping. **Global Warm** sets the default count and timing (**Auto**, **Fixed 4 / 9 / 15 min**, or **Custom 1–60 min**) for chats that haven't picked their own. Turning warming off for a chat silences its expiry and limit desktop alerts. Desktop alerts for stalled chats are also off by default and can be enabled separately. Each warm-up asks the model for a short `OK` reply and uses input tokens (or the full conversation if the cache already expired). The panel also controls desktop alerts, pausing protection, local cleanup, and file-size limits. Preset modes & tool-loading modes via CLI: ```bash node scripts/install.mjs mode host-45k # Default: direct read up to 45 KB code / 128 KB patches, block >16 KB noisy logs node scripts/install.mjs mode balanced-16k # Outline first above 16 KB node scripts/install.mjs mode fast-32k # Raise normal file limit to 32 KB node scripts/install.mjs mode strict-8k # Block above 8 KB node scripts/install.mjs mode no-read-hook # Never block file reads, only trim noisy terminal output node scripts/install.mjs tool-loading fast-eager # Default: 4 fast tools eager, 8 context tools lazy node scripts/install.mjs tool-loading lazy # All 12 tools lazy-loaded node scripts/install.mjs tool-loading eager # All 12 tools eager-loaded ``` > **Troubleshooting (`ide-tools` duplicate `/required` error):** If Antigravity fails during toolbox initialization with `building toolbox: tool "mcp_ide-tools_mcp_agy-dart_fast_apply_edits" advertises an invalid parameter schema ... at '/required': items at 1 and 2 are equal`, the host's `ide-tools` bridge is re-wrapping already-eager `mcp_agy-dart_fast_*` tools and appending `toolSummary` to `/required` a second time without deduplicating (`agy-dart` itself only declares `"required": ["edits"]`). Switch to lazy loading and restart Antigravity: > > ```bash > node ~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-dart/scripts/install.mjs tool-loading lazy > ``` > > (Or remove `"tools"` / `"eager": true` under `mcpServers.fast` in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/agy-dart/mcp_config.json` and restart. See [skills/agy-dart/references/error-playbook.md](skills/agy-dart/references/error-playbook.md) for diagnostics.) --- ## Changelog ### v1.7.8 - **Opt-in silent auto-updates (default OFF)**: Added an `Auto-Update: OFF/ON` toggle in the dashboard topbar (also configurable via `autoUpdateInstall` in `~/.agy-dart/config.json` or `AGY_DART_AUTO_UPDATE_INSTALL` / `AGY_DART_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE_INSTALL`). --- ## 这个 Google Antigravity 插件是干什么的？ `agy-dart` 是专为 **Google Antigravity** 打造的性能、缓存与上下文管理插件（同时支持通过 `--target` 安装到 DeepSeek Harness、Claude Code 与 Codex）：减少重复读取和过长的工具输出，查看缓存用量，会话占满上下文或卡住时可以把进度带到新对话。 装好之后在后台自动生效，不用记新命令，平时照常打字聊天就行： ### 1. 整合动作 AI 要搜好几个词时一次同时搜完，要改多个文件时一次改完并顺手跑完测试，少跑好几轮重复带上下文的请求。 ### 2. 挡住废话 跑一次测试吐出 3000 行日志，插件只挑关键那几句给 AI（比如第 42 行报错，其余 199 个通过），完整原文存进本地备查。遇到几千行的大代码文件，先拉目录再读要改的那几十行。 ### 3. 缓存监测与按需续温 插件在客户端侧稳定可控前缀，并减少短时间内重复读取未修改的文件；实际缓存命中率仍取决于宿主构造请求的方式及后端缓存行为（若排查动态代理分流影响，可固定单一出口作为有对照的排查实验）。自动续温和缓存到期桌面提醒默认关闭。首次开启续温时，每段对话最多自动请求 1 次，发新消息后重新计数。次数可在面板里调整。 ### 4. 右侧面板与崩溃/卡死抢救 右侧边栏面板直接显示：上下文还有多少、缓存还剩几分钟过期、挡掉了多少废话。 多开项目窗口时，哪个后台窗口上下文快满了，或者一直转圈不出字，右下角会弹窗标明是哪个窗口、哪段对话，点一下弹窗直接切过去。会话真因为爆上下文崩掉或卡死时，在面板点一下复制当前进度摘要，贴到新对话接着往下做。 ### 其他内置功能 1. **压缩对话（`/compact`）后恢复上下文线索**：后台记录本轮改过哪些文件、最近一次测试或打包过没过、存过哪些参考资料。跑完 `/compact` 后 AI 可以直接调出这份记录接着做。 2. **长文档与网页存本地检索**：几万字的开发文档或网页可以先按章节存进本地数据库，后面用到哪段按关键词搜哪段。 3. **大日志与大表格先在本地跑脚本筛选**：遇到几十 MB 的日志、CSV 或几万行 JSON，AI 可以在本地沙盒跑几行脚本先做统计（比如筛出报错最多的 5 个接口），只把算出来的结果发回对话；大 JSON 还会自动摘出报错的异常条。 4. **新对话自动附带目录结构**：刚开对话时自动给出一份精简的项目目录、脚本和核心文件清单。 5. **死循环提示**：AI 连续出现「改代码 → 报错 → 改回去 → --- ## What does this Google Antigravity plugin do? `agy-dart` is a performance, KV-cache, and context-window plugin for **Google Antigravity** (also supports DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, and Codex via `--target`). It reduces repeated reads and large tool results, shows prompt-cache usage, and helps you resume work in a new chat when a session fills up or stalls. Once installed, it runs automatically in the background — no new commands to learn, just chat and code as usual: ### 1. Combine actions When the AI needs to search several terms, it runs them in one batch; when it edits multiple files, it edits them together and runs tests in the same step instead of resending your full chat context across half a dozen turns. ### 2. Block noise If a test run prints 3,000 lines of logs, the plugin passes only the lines that matter to the AI (e.g., line 42 failed, the other 199 passed) and stores the full log locally for lookup. On multi-thousand-line code files, it pulls the outline first and reads only the target lines. ### 3. Cache monitoring and optional keepalive The plugin stabilizes controllable client-side prefixes and reduces repeated reads of unchanged files; actual cache hit rates still depend on how the host constructs requests and on backend caching behavior (if you use a dynamic proxy pool, pinning a single exit node can serve as a controlled troubleshooting experiment). Automatic keepalive and desktop expiry alerts start off. If you enable keepalive, the initial limit is one ping per chat until your next message. You can change the limit in the panel. ### 4. Side panel & crash/hang rescue The right-sidebar panel shows: remaining context space, minutes until cache expiry, and total noise blocked. With multiple project windows open, if a background window is nearly out of context or stuck spinning with zero output, a desktop popup names that exact project and chat — click the popup to jump straight there. If a session crashes from blown-out context or hangs completely, click once in the panel to copy a progress summary and paste it into a new chat to continue. ### Other built-in features 1. **Restore context clues after `/compact`**: Records modified files, latest test/build pass status, and saved reference IDs in the background so the AI can pick back up right after `/compact`. 2. **Local search for long docs & web pages**: Stores multi-thousand-word docs or web pages by section in a local database and fetches only matching sections by keyword. 3. **Local script filtering for giant logs & tables**: On multi-MB logs, CSVs, or huge JSON dumps, the AI runs a short local script to compute counts or extract rows (e.g., top 5 failing endpoints) and returns only the result; large JSON outputs also surface error rows automatically. 4. **Workspace layout on new chats**: Supplies a compact directory, script, and core-file summary at the start of a new conversation. 5. **Loop warnings**: Shows a UI-only note (not injected into model context) when the AI repeats `edit → fail → revert → fail` cycles or calls the same tool with no progress. 6. **Secret masking & sensitive-file blocking**: Masks API keys and tokens in logs or fetched pages, blocks accidental reads of `.env` files when configured, and sandboxes read-only `git` queries against untrusted `.git/config` hooks. 7. **Hard 8.8 KB response cap with dynamic quota**: Antigravity spills tool outputs above ~10 KB into a temp file that costs an extra read turn; all plugin responses stay within 8.8 KB, dynamically giving short passing checks' unused space to failing stack traces. 8. **Detailed panel breakdown & offline simulation**: Inspect context usage across file reads, terminal output, and subagents, check 15-turn cache hit trends and miss causes, optionally read only changed lines after edits (off by default), or replay past chat history via CLI to measure cache hit rates and keepalive cost. 9. **Works smoothly alongside your Skills, plus a Skills bloat check**: Use it with any Skills in Antigravity, Claude Code, or Codex — your Skills guide the workflow while `agy-dart` quietly blocks giant file reads, trims noisy logs, and looks after your cache; run `node bin/agy-dart.mjs audit skills` to see how much startup context each installed Skill uses and spot oversized main files. > Antigravity updates frequently — click **Star** at the top right to follow compatibility updates. --- ## How to Install Use **Node.js 22.16.0 or later in the 22.x line, or Node.js 24 or later**.
